clue.text: Mark setting the standard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a version of a product, as in a Mark II car
second meaning: exemplary, fit to be copied

explanation.surface: A grade or score that sets the benchmark for everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a score, but here it is a design version, like the Mark II of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular design or version of a manufactured item is called a model, and as an adjective the word means perfect, exemplary, worth copying.

clue.text: With oil streaming out, this prospector is made

indicators.note: something streaming out flows loose and scattered, so the letters before it are let free to be rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A prospector strikes oil and, as it gushes out, becomes a rich man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streaming' does double duty: it is fodder and, with 'out', the signal. The surface 'made' means made rich; a prospector who studies rocks is a MINERALOGIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies rocks and ores is the kind of expert who would search the ground for valuable deposits.

clue.text: Forces abroad, for example

parts.note: surface reading: troops stationed overseas, a noun phrase
setter's reading: a verb, compels something to move elsewhere, such as away to another country

explanation.surface: Military forces serving overseas, given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks like a noun for the armed services; it is a verb, and sending someone abroad is one example of moving them out of their place.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel a person or thing to leave its usual position and move somewhere else is to displace it.

clue.text: Pull in here, set down and bid farewell

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down
a variant spelling of bye, as in by-by, a word used to say goodbye

explanation.surface: Someone told to pull in, put something down and say goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside parking strip where drivers can stop off the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside parking area is exactly the place where a motorist pulls over and stops off the carriageway.

clue.text: Wrong leader's taken on top dog

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or top, with the 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the word after it is to be put in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The wrong leader has been put in charge of the top dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' wants to be one phrase; 'top' gives A1 (first-class), written AI, and 'dog' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed originally from Yorkshire, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: Turns away from little green man, hair standing on end

parts.note: the cartoon image of a visitor from space

indicators.note: in a down entry, something standing on end is turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a seta is a stiff hair or bristle, as on an insect

explanation.surface: A frightened person recoils from a little green man whose hair stands up on end.
explanation.walkthrough: SETA, a biological word for a bristle, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people is to estrange them and make them unfriendly, so it means driving them away or making them turn from you.

clue.text: Pound from base limit bouncing back to upper limit

indicators.note: a ball bouncing back travels the opposite way, so what is left is read backwards
taking one thing from another means removing it, so the first item is lost from the second

parts.note: a floor is a lower limit, as in a price floor
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra; it is removed

explanation.surface: A price that bounces from its bottom level up to the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: Floor and roof are the paired lower and upper limits, as in price floors and spending roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof is the top covering of a building, and figuratively a ceiling or maximum level that cannot be exceeded.

clue.text: Blue ? Tory out and out

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling down
the Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A true-blue Conservative, thoroughly committed.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the Conservative Party colour, which makes 'Blue' look political; it means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions describe something complete and utter, as in a downright lie or an out-and-out lie.

clue.text: Extract of poplar, chestnut, box and conifer

indicators.note: an extract is a part drawn out of a whole, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: running across the end of the first tree name and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A list of trees: poplar, chestnut, box and a conifer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is padding that keeps the list of trees going; the letters come only from the first two names.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a cone-bearing tree, unusual among them for shedding its needles each winter.

clue.text: Bad lot? Bad job!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an unpleasant, untrustworthy person
second meaning, taken literally: an unpleasant piece of labour

explanation.surface: An exasperated verdict on a shoddy result.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a mean, disagreeable person, while read literally it is a disagreeable task, so it fits both phrases.

clue.text: Quality of the candid camera photo?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a photographic slide viewed by light shining through it

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a Candid Camera snapshot special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'candid camera' runs together as the name of a hidden-camera TV show, but the clue splits between those two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Openness and honesty are the traits of frank people, and a positive slide or film for projecting is also given this name.

clue.text: Partner wearing girdle with ribbing

indicators.note: a person wearing something has it around them, so one item sits inside the other

parts.note: a ring is a band that encircles, like a girdle
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A partner putting on a girdle and getting teased for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying is an old-fashioned word for good-humoured teasing or banter, which is what ribbing someone means.

clue.text: Chief meeting Queen's man with bow

parts.note: arch- means chief, as in archbishop or arch-enemy
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A chief encounters the Queen's courtier, who bows to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man with bow' suggests a courtier bowing to royalty; the bow is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots arrows using a bow, so a man carrying one describes him.

clue.text: Spike tears dreadfully

parts.note: to spike a drink is to lace it with alcohol

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly and messily, so the word before it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spike rips something horribly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: a spike tears flesh dreadfully, which is what LACERATES means.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to cut or rip skin roughly and deeply, a ragged and violent kind of tearing.

clue.text: Return to gold standard and mint, say

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the next two words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
or is gold in heraldry
standard, as in a stock answer

explanation.surface: An economic proposal to return to the gold standard and its coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold standard' and 'mint' paint a monetary picture, but mint is the herb, which spreads by underground stems.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a plant that grows from a creeping rhizome, the underground stem botanists also call by this name.

clue.text: Pair of cords to go with brogues, perhaps

definitions.text: Pair of cords to go with brogues, perhaps

parts.words: Pair of cords to go with brogues
parts.note: surface reading: a pair of corduroy trousers to wear with smart shoes
setter's reading: two strings that fasten each shoe, brogues being one example of footwear

explanation.surface: Choosing corduroy trousers to match a pair of brogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cords' suggests corduroy trousers; they are literal strings. Brogues are sturdy leather shoes with decorative perforations.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the thin strings threaded through eyelets to tie footwear on, and they are sold in pairs.

clue.text: Character going to seed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: innate nature or temperament
second meaning: a single seed of a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Someone whose character is going to seed, falling into decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to seed' reads as an idiom for deterioration; here 'going to' only joins two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain can mean a person's natural disposition, and it is also the small hard fruit of wheat, rice or similar cereals.

clue.text: A new wine list introduced ahead of starters

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does, and to tip is the same
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A new wine list is brought out before the first courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wine list' wants to be read as a menu; 'list' is the verb meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian appetisers served before the main meal, so they are starters in the dining sense.

clue.text: Heartless visitor saw round to our delight

indicators.note: without a heart means the central part is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: a guest is a visitor; its middle letter goes
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted visitor came round, much to our delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is keen enjoyment or relish in doing something, close in meaning to delight.

clue.text: Baseball player in pants and T-shirt

parts.note: pants here are short trousers
a T-shirt is a top

explanation.surface: A baseball player dressed casually in pants and a T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball the shortstop fields between second and third base.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop is the infielder positioned between second and third base, one of nine fielding positions.

clue.text: Hack covers page with sensational headline

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps round it, so one item goes inside the other

parts.note: to hack is to slash or cut
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A journalist covers a page story with an eye-catching headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a tabloid journalist, fitting the newspaper scene; it is the verb to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is newspaper slang for the big front-page story given prominent, sensational display.

clue.text: Girl, if topless, would create an atmosphere

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so being topless means losing it

parts.note: an aura is the distinctive atmosphere around a person or place; it is what remains once the top letter goes

explanation.surface: A girl who goes topless would certainly change the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: remove the first letter of the girl's name and AURA is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura is a female given name, and crosswords use girl to signal a first name.

clue.text: Clever daily means to fix the buzzer

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or knowing
a daily is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A smart newspaper solution for repairing a doorbell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzer' and 'fix' suggest repairing a bell; the buzzer is a fly, and to fix it is to stick it fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is a sticky strip that traps insects, holding the buzzing pest fast so it cannot escape.

clue.text: Some encouragement, you say, is in vain

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: a prod is a nudge of encouragement

indicators.note: to say is to speak, so the word before it is turned into a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like this word

explanation.surface: Someone saying that a little praise is wasted effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in vain' reads as futile; 'is in' is the container signal and 'vain' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vain person has an excessively high opinion of themselves, and proud means conceited in the same way.

clue.text: Ice in the drink?

parts.note: surface reading: ice cubes in a cocktail
setter's reading: the drink is slang for the sea, so this is floating ice at sea

explanation.surface: Asking for ice in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is informal for the sea, so the ice is a floating mass, short for iceberg.
explanation.definitionFit: This short form names a large floating mass of ice that has broken off a glacier into the sea.

clue.text: Set opening clue, working to mislead

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
the first clue of a crossword is usually one across
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A setter writes the first clue, aiming to throw solvers off.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes crossword setting itself: the surface setter writing the first clue is exactly someone trying to mislead solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deceive or trick someone, getting something past them, which is to mislead.

clue.text: Period of ignorance without the Sun and Times?

parts.note: with no sunlight it is dark
times as in eras or ages

explanation.surface: An era with no Sun or Times newspapers, a time when nobody knew anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and The Times are British newspapers, so the surface pictures a news blackout leaving everyone uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval era in Europe is traditionally seen as a time of lost learning and little culture.

clue.text: Girl to coordinate going on stage

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform or stage
y is a coordinate in algebra, alongside x

explanation.surface: A girl taking charge of organising things as she goes on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coordinate' reads as a verb, organise; it is the noun, the y-coordinate on a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Daisy is a female first name, and crosswords use girl to signal a given name.
